Team — draft points to include in the final narrative and SIG mapping (I captured them inline below; edit and push comments):

On Tue, Aug 22, 2026 at 9:12 AM Alice Miller <alice.miller@greystone.com> wrote:
> - A short network diagram (PNG/PDF) showing control-plane endpoints, management plane, and customer data plane separation for both Dedicated and Private modes.
> - Answers in SIG mapping format to Qs about control-plane isolation, KV/cache segmentation, and how KMS keys and audit logs are scoped per customer.

Draft narrative (summary bullets):
- Control-plane isolation: Redwood runs a logically separated control plane in the Redwood management VPC; for Dedicated customers we provision dedicated management subnets that are logically isolated via tenant-specific routing and security groups. For Private (VPC-onboarded) customers control-plane proxies are mounted into the customer's VPC via private peering or customer-managed transit; control-plane control traffic uses mTLS between services and is restricted to management CIDRs.
- KV/cache segmentation: All KV and inference cache is tenant-scoped. Dedicated pools run per-tenant cache instances backed by isolated memory/GPU-local caches; Private connectors never share an in-memory KV across tenants. Cache eviction and prefix-tracking metadata are sharded by tenant-id to preclude cross-tenant key collisions.
- KMS & audit: We support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed KMS. When Greystone requests customer-managed keys, we create per-tenant key bindings and restrict key use to that tenant's control-plane project. Audit logs for control-plane actions are written to customer-scoped logging projects and retained per the contract (default 90 days, configurable).
- Egress: By default no control-plane egress to public internet occurs; control-plane traffic stays within provider private backbone or customer VPC. When small outbound flows are required (updates, telemetry) they traverse dedicated NATs with strict egress ACLs and are sent to allowlisted endpoints only.
- Lifecycle runbook (provision/decommission): we include a 6-step lifecycle: (1) tenant claim + id, (2) allocate management project and KMS binding, (3) provision compute pool (dedicated/private connector), (4) apply routing and policy, (5) test and harden, (6) decommission + key-rotation + data-sweep. Each step is auditable and generates an acquisition/deletion event in the audit log.

Attachments to produce: annotated topology PNG (kimberly), SIG answers XLSX (jonas), lifecycle checklist (marcus). I'll assemble after reviews.
